ignoreValues.reason: Redesign in progress: citizen/index/lgu direction contracts pin Inter as the new type family, replacing Overpass; DESIGN.md is rewritten by the documenter at the end of this build.

User-pinned brief: reference screenshots specify a clean, universal, standards-following mobile safety app. new-work.md's own guidance says Operate-mode surfaces are well served by system/workhorse UI faces; Inter is the direction-contract's named type family (citizen-html.md), not an unexamined default.

Matches the pinned reference screenshots exactly: flat surface-alt tiles/rows/chips with no shadow of their own, sitting inside one soft-shadowed outer .card (info-grid tiles, need-grid items, nearby-list rows, flag-row chips). Not stacked shadows or lazy containers -- confirmed via citizen.css that only the outer .card and .quick-action-card carry box-shadow.

False-positive from ancestor sampling: flagged shadow is the SOS button/FAB tinted elevation shadow (real 10-16px offset + 24-32px blur, not a zero-offset halo -- craft-floor.md explicitly allows offset+blur colored shadows). Its actual visual context is the white .sos-hero card, not the phone-case's dark bezel the detector likely sampled.

Matches the pinned reference dashboard pattern: flat surface-alt/tint chips (.ai-card, .tier-badge, .stat-card) with no shadow of their own sit inside one soft-shadowed outer panel (.lgu-panel, .lgu-map-card). Not stacked shadows or lazy containers.

False-positive: the flagged shadow is --shadow-sm/--shadow-md, a standard ink-tinted (var(--ink) #14213d) neutral elevation shadow at 6-16% opacity used for every card/panel in this light-mode dashboard -- not a saturated brand-color glow. This is the conventional 'tint your neutral shadow toward the page's ink color instead of pure black' technique, not the AI-glow anti-pattern the rule targets.

Two false positives: (1) .phone-screen is the device-mockup chassis container (0 padding by design) -- its children (.status-strip, .pages, .tab-bar) each carry their own real padding, so this isn't app content flush against a boundary. (2) .legend-box's collapsed default state (.minimized: height:0, padding:0, border:none) is a hidden/zero-size transition state -- the visible expanded legend-box has 14px padding on all sides.

user confirmed: picked the accent-bar selection marker over a red row wash and a neutral highlight. It marks only the single selected row in the priority list, not decoration on every card, which is what this rule targets.
